tagline: Land held in common, kept for good
sector: A small accredited land trust that holds conservation easements and stewards preserves in one Connecticut valley, funded by a few hundred local giving households.
founded_place_size: Founded 1994, based in the Sedgewater valley, Litchfield County, Connecticut. Four staff, roughly nine hundred acres under easement, a few hundred giving households.
about: Rivermeadow protects the meadows, hollows and river bends of one valley by holding easements and caring for a handful of small preserves. Many of our donors granted the land we now steward, so the relationship is personal and long. We exist so the fields stay fields for the people who walk them.
audience: Local giving households aged 45 to 78, land literate, many of them easement grantors who know the fields by name. Gifts run from 25 dollars to 25,000, a broad community base plus a small leadership circle that carries most of the campaign.
price_positioning: A community land trust, not a national charity. Two registers live in one base: a warm community of small and mid gifts, and a leadership circle giving four and five figures. Every dollar should read as spent on the land, not on ourselves.

palette.name: River Slate
palette.usage: The trust mark recovered from the Fenn Hollow plaque, the letterhead wordmark, the header rule and the signatory's name: wordmark, rule and signatory as on rivermeadow_letter_community.pdf and rivermeadow_letter_leadership.pdf, wordmark and rule as on rivermeadow_receipt.pdf. It may also set the donor household name. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Meadow Green
palette.usage: The tagline, small labels such as NAME & ADDRESS and GIFT SUMMARY on rivermeadow_receipt.pdf, and the river of the trust mark. Never a ground, panel, letter text or receipt text.

palette.name: Heron Grey
palette.usage: Hairline keylines around a photograph, as on rivermeadow_letter_leadership.pdf and rivermeadow_receipt.pdf. Never a ground, panel or type colour.

palette.name: Bronze Patina
palette.role: mandatory wherever a giving level name appears, so on every letter
palette.usage: Giving level names only, set in Chivo Bold capitals as the type system requires. Never a ground, panel, rule, body text or the mark.

palette.name: Cream Stock
palette.usage: The ground of every letter, as on rivermeadow_letter_community.pdf and rivermeadow_letter_leadership.pdf. A receipt may use it or the unprinted white of rivermeadow_receipt.pdf. Never a type colour.

palette.name: Field Ink
palette.usage: The salutation, the letter paragraphs and amounts, as on rivermeadow_letter_community.pdf and rivermeadow_letter_leadership.pdf; the address, the gift summary lines and the statutory wording, as on rivermeadow_receipt.pdf; and the address and gift count on a letter. It may also set the donor household name. Never a ground or panel.

typography: Rivermeadow Trust sets Chivo against Adobe Caslon Pro. Step 01, the donor household name, is Chivo Light at 30 pt on 33 pt with 0.01 em negative tracking, standing alone above the salutation as the largest thing on the sheet. Step 02, the giving level name, is Chivo Bold capitals at 11 pt on 13 pt tracked 0.18 em in Bronze Patina. Step 03, the letter, is Adobe Caslon Pro Regular at 11 pt on 15.5 pt, tracking 0, a maximum of 65 characters a line, and 18 px on 28 px on the web. Step 04, the statutory receipt wording, is Adobe Caslon Pro Regular at 8.5 pt on 12 pt tracked 0.02 em, a size supplied here because the prose gives none, with receipt amounts holding at 12 pt with tabular figures. Letter headings set Adobe Caslon Pro Semibold at 16 pt on 19 pt, and nothing on the sheet, heading, amount or giving level, is ever allowed to outsize the donor name.
voice: Plain, grateful and specific, the voice of a neighbour rather than an institution. It names the field, not the fund. Example: We kept forty more acres in hay this year because you asked us to.
brand_assets_status: The original logo files left with our first designer and are gone. The mark now survives only on the cast bronze donor plaque at the Fenn Hollow trailhead, of which we hold one photograph. Approved letter copy, giving level names and thresholds, and the statutory receipt wording still exist as plain text.
values: Permanence of the land, and a personal duty of thanks to every household that gives, whatever the size of the gift.

rules: Never let a heading outsize a donor name.
The donor household name stands alone above the salutation at 30 pt and is the largest thing on the sheet.
Giving level names set Chivo Bold capitals at 11 pt tracked 0.18 em in Bronze Patina.
Letter headings set Adobe Caslon Pro Semibold at 16 pt.
Receipt amounts set at 12 pt with tabular figures.
Approved letter copy, giving level names and thresholds, and the statutory receipt wording are used exactly as written.
Web sets the letter at 18 px on 28 px.
Every dollar should read as spent on the land, not on ourselves: no treatment that looks like a national charity's.

palette_rules.distribution: Every letter sits on a Cream Stock ground; a receipt sits on Cream Stock or the unprinted white of the paper, as on rivermeadow_receipt.pdf. No colour forms any other ground, panel or band. Field Ink sets the salutation, letter paragraphs, amounts, addresses, gift counts, gift summary lines and statutory wording. River Slate sets the trust mark, letterhead wordmark, header rule and signatory's name. The donor household name is Field Ink or River Slate. Bronze Patina sets giving level names and nothing else. Meadow Green (tagline, small labels, the river of the trust mark) and Heron Grey (keylines around photographs) together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: a photograph sits in its frame with no fade into the ground.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, rules, keylines, panels or the mark. No metallic, foil, gloss, emboss or bevel effect on any type, rule or mark, Bronze Patina included: every dollar should read as spent on the land, not on a national charity's treatment.
palette_rules.photography: Preserve photographs keep their own colour and are never tinted, duotoned or recoloured toward the palette. A frame may be straightened or cropped, but not recoloured.
